key_insight: Raising the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio made Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings denser and better bonded, with the best overall surface/adhesion performance at 1.2.
engineering_relevance: Process-gas tuning in flame spraying is an effective control knob for optimizing coating quality on corrosion-resistant steel parts.
method: Deposited Ni–Cr–B–Si coatings on AISI 321 steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II flame-spray system.
Varied the O2/C2H2 ratio to 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 and monitored spray conditions with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured porosity, microhardness, roughness, and adhesion strength to compare coating quality.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports porosity dropping from 1.97% to 0.90%, roughness from 4.70 to 2.99 μm, and adhesion rising from 22.14 to 35.02 MPa, with peak microhardness of 1051.7 HV at O2/C2H2 = 1.1.
watch_item: These results are parameter- and system-specific, so the optimal gas ratio may shift with powder feed, torch setup, substrate condition, or post-spray treatment.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
